dress_code.title: Temple Dress Code
dress_code.description: Guidelines for respectful clothing when visiting religious and cultural places in Sri Lanka.
guidance: Wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees.
Avoid shorts, mini skirts, and sleeveless tops.
White or light-colored clothing is preferred at many temples.
Remove hats, caps, and sunglasses before entering sacred places.
Carry a shawl or scarf if unsure about dress appropriateness.

etiquette.title: Religious Etiquette
etiquette.description: Behavior guidance for tourists visiting sacred and cultural places.
guidance: Remove shoes before entering temple areas.
Speak quietly and respectfully.
Respect worshippers and religious ceremonies.
Do not touch monks unnecessarily.
Do not point feet toward Buddha statues.
Stand respectfully when religious rituals are happening.

photography_rules.title: Photography Guidance
photography_rules.description: Important photography etiquette for sacred places and cultural events.
guidance: Ask permission before taking photos of people.
Avoid disrespectful selfies with Buddha statues.
Flash photography may not be allowed indoors.
Some temples prohibit photography in sacred areas.
Respect signs indicating photography restrictions.
avoid: Turning your back toward Buddha statues in selfies

language_phrase.title: Useful Local Phrases
language_phrase.description: Basic Sinhala and Tamil phrases helpful for tourists in Sri Lanka.
guidance: Ayubowan = Hello / Greetings (Sinhala)
Istuti = Thank you (Sinhala)
Vanakkam = Hello (Tamil)
Nandri = Thank you (Tamil)
Using local greetings is appreciated by Sri Lankans.

festival_guidance.title: Festival Guidance
festival_guidance.description: Cultural awareness tips during Sri Lankan festivals and religious events.
guidance: Dress modestly during festivals.
Follow crowd control and safety instructions.
Respect religious processions and rituals.
Arrive early for major events due to crowds.
Keep public spaces clean during celebrations.
